images.prompt: Premium editorial photograph, high-end tech magazine style: a network closet seen straight on with its door open. A patch panel occupies the upper half, densely populated with cables that all sweep downward and converge into a single switch below it: many above, one path out, the bundle narrowing dramatically as it descends. The closet interior is lit soft cream from a single overhead fitting; the room beyond the open door is deep navy and empty. CRITICAL COLOUR RULE: there are NO indicator lights, NO status LEDs and NO lamps anywhere in this photograph. Every port, panel and device is completely unlit and dark, with no points of light of any colour. The only red in the entire frame is ONE SINGLE RED PATCH CABLE running through the bundle among all the others, which are cream coloured. That one red cable is a physical cable, not a light. Nothing else anywhere is red. Absolutely no text, no letterforms, no numerals, no labels, no cable tags, no port numbering, no panel legends, no signage, no logos, no vendor marks on any faceplate, panel or cable. Deep dark navy (#161a45) dominates every surface and every background plane, never blue, never cyan, no teal, never slate blue or blue-grey, and never neutral grey, charcoal, black or silver. Navy must be obvious at a glance. Soft cream (#F4EFE3) is the only highlight. Full-bleed edge-to-edge artwork: no border, no cream margin, no white matting, no picture frame. No glow effects, no light rays, no floating particles. Realistic photography, shallow depth of field, cinematic moody lighting, minimalist composition.
images.usage: Facebook + X (16:9). LinkedIn and Instagram take the full 10-slide carousel.
images.qa:
Approved on the THIRD roll, and the rejections are the useful part.

hero-01 put a row of red port LEDs across the switch front panel, with the 'exactly one red' guard already present and the permitted object named. It also came back as flat vector illustration rather than photography.

hero-02 moved the switch lights off successfully but rendered THREE red indicator lamps on the patch panel, having been asked for one solitary lamp.

hero-03 abandoned indicator lights entirely: the prompt turns every light in the scene off and gives the accent to a single red patch cable among cream ones. That worked first time, and it is also the better image — the red cable runs the length of the converging bundle, so the accent carries the argument instead of sitting in a corner.

**Standing lesson, confirmed four times now:** the 'exactly one red element' guard works when red is carried by a distinct physical object, and fails when it is carried by an indicator LED. The generator honours WHICH object may be red but not HOW MANY instances when the object is a small repeated light. Nov 4, Nov 8 and both earlier rolls here all failed the same way. When a scene contains equipment, do not ask for one lit indicator — switch every light off in the prompt and give the accent to something physical.

The no-labels clause held on all three rolls, which matters: a patch panel is the most label-prone subject briefed so far and nothing leaked.
